claim_ceiling: Two new benchmarks (citation proximity, legal-area clustering) execute and produce interpretable results on real BGer corpus. TF-IDF baseline fails both benchmarks, establishing clear targets for legal-distance lane.
evidence_summary: Internal consistency verification confirms both new benchmarks execute correctly on 1,200 real BGer decisions. Citation proximity: AUC-ROC 0.6354 (FAILED, threshold 0.7), positive_mean_sim 0.187 > negative_mean_sim 0.127, gap 0.060. Legal-area clustering: NMI 0.0487 (FAILED, threshold 0.3), purity 0.7046 (borderline), best at k=12 clusters. Both results are internally consistent and match expected TF-IDF characteristics: partial lexical overlap for citation proximity, language-dominated clustering for legal-area. No data leakage (TF-IDF on text, citations/branches from metadata), benchmark gaming (thresholds pre-declared), post-hoc metrics, weak baselines, boilerplate confounding, visual-prettiness bias, or unsupported claims detected. Two minor issues: branch distribution labeling shows full corpus (1200) not sampled (400), and report recommends tighter targets than frozen criteria. Honest negative/null work correctly identifies TF-IDF limitations. Claim ceiling appropriately bounded to benchmark establishment.
